body:
This sounds like a strong candidate for a before/after serialization diff. If possible, attach a minimal project with the `.tscn` or `.tres` after the first save and after a few repeated parameter edits, even if the file is trimmed to the relevant `FontVariation` resource block.

That would help distinguish whether stale glyph cache data is being appended on save, duplicated when the built-in resource is externalized, or regenerated from editor-side preview state.

Apologies for the confusion earlier, the bloating is incredibly aggressive! 

I managed to capture the sequential growth by doing a strict, controlled test. I simply created an empty scene, used a lightweight English font, made the `FontVariation` built-in (via "Make Unique"), and strictly tweaked the Embolden slider only once per save. 

The file sizes skyrocketed exponentially:
1. `01_first_save_no_tweak.tscn` -> 1,109 KB (Right after clicking "Make Unique")
2. `02_after_1_tweak.tscn` -> 4,041 KB (After tweaking the slider once and saving)
3. `03_after_2_tweak.tscn` -> 11,631 KB (After tweaking the slider a second time and saving)

I have attached a zip file containing these 3 `.tscn` stages below. You can easily diff them to see exactly how the glyph cache data is exponentially duplicating inside the built-in resource block upon each serialization.

[font-variation-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29351859/font-variation-test.zip)

Hope this provides the perfect before/after diff for investigation!
